(3) Do tallies MATERIALISE into the .dd.json, or exist only in the rendered .dd.md? Reported WITH its workaround rather than instead of it, which is the standing consumer rule working as intended, and the first live instance of R-4a. | ready | s | nothing — ruled by o-prime 2026-08-09; no urgency for plan 080 (koala's workaround holds and its fork is deleted in phase 3), matters for every other consumer of the standalone CLI | pij-related-koala (found and reported it, with the workaround disclosed); pij-certain-crab (reproduced on a minimal fixture, found the rm one-way door and the shared-reason-code root cause); pij-mental-dajeil (the field-versus-section probe that decided it) | THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT, and it is stronger than anything either seat reasoned to: DD ALREADY HAS IMPLICIT-CREATE SEMANTICS AT THE FIELD LEVEL AND HAS SHIPPED THEM ALL ALONG. One fixture, one schema, one verb, two levels — `dd set d.dd.json#notes` on a declared-but-absent SECTION refuses E450, while `dd set d.dd.json#rows/r-1/note hello` on a declared-but-absent FIELD returns ok and `dd get` then shows {id: r-1, note: hello}. Same "declared but not yet instantiated" state, opposite answers. SO IMPLICIT CREATE IS NOT A WIDENING OF THE WRITER CONTRACT, IT IS THE REMOVAL OF AN INCONSISTENCY — which inverts the strongest objection against it (that `set` on a declared-but-misspelled name would create rather than refuse: that is ALREADY LIVE for fields and evidently acceptable). Consistency can only resolve one way, because the other direction — refusing absent fields too — would break every consumer setting an optional field on an existing row, which is ordinary use. ROOT CAUSE: src/mutate/locate.ts refuses at :33 (`schema declares no section X` — genuinely unknown) and at :36 (`the document has no section X` — declared, creatable) with THE SAME reason code `section-unknown`, the same E450/DD_MUTATION_TARGET_INVALID, and the same next_action. The two states differ only in free-text prose, so a machine consumer must string-match the message to tell "does not exist" from "not created yet" — the exact failure the envelope exists to prevent, and one this repository refuses in three other places. At :36 the declaration is already in hand and is discarded. RULED (o-prime, 2026-08-09), three parts: (1) SPLIT THE REASON CODES — unconditional, ship it even if the rest is deferred, and the next_action must differ too (`dd schema show` is correct for genuinely-unknown and a CIRCLE for declared-but-absent, since it displays the very declaration the refusal denies). (2) IMPLICIT CREATE on set/add for a declared section — validation already runs pre-write, so a created section is schema-checked exactly like any other mutation. (3) NO `dd section add` verb — it would add public surface for something set/add already mean, and the curated-surface ruling of the same morning says every addition is an API review; this one does not earn it. |
| wl-0018 | A proxied registry makes local `npm audit` systematically more OPTIMISTIC than reality | Measured 2026-08-09 by two seats independently. | wl-0019 | An unrecognised relation degrades to `ref` in silence — on TWO paths, with opposite risk profiles | `src/core/rel.ts:24` is `isBuiltinRel(rel) ? rel : DEFAULT_REL`, and there is NO diagnostic anywhere for an unrecognised rel — three comments document the intent, none reports it. Every one of those silently switches OFF contradiction detection for that edge, and nothing anywhere says so. THE CAPITALISED SPELLING IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: it is not a typo a reviewer notices, it reads as correct, and its effect is to disable the one inconsistency a plan document can prove about itself. This reaches every consumer — `satisfies` and BUILTIN_RELS live in src/core/constants.ts, which SHIPS; the contradiction engine that consumes them is in src/plan/, which does NOT (no ./plan in the exports map). (1) DECLARE CUSTOM RELS IN THE SCHEMA — closes it completely and keeps the namespace open, at the price of authoring burden and a schema change; an undeclared rel then becomes a genuine finding rather than a guess. (2) WARN ON A NEAR-MISS TO A BUILTIN — cheap and needs no schema change, but it is a HEURISTIC, and a heuristic guard is a new class of thing in this repository, where every other gate is exact. It would also not catch a rel that is simply invented and wrong in a way no builtin resembles. NEITHER IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT ON n=1, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A ROW. THE CLASS, which is the reason to keep it: an unrecognised key silently discarded is the same defect `pij-related-meadowlark` reported in `sanitizeDdLink` in another repository in the same week — two codebases, one week, one shape. AND IT IS THIS PLAN'S PARENT CAUSE IN THE RELATION VOCABULARY: one observable, two meanings, with nothing in the output to separate them. The general rule it argues for: WHEN A SYSTEM DEGRADES AN INPUT IT DOES NOT RECOGNISE, THE DEGRADATION MUST BE VISIBLE SOMEWHERE, OR THE MOST DANGEROUS INPUT IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS CORRECT. CORRECTED THE SAME HOUR, BY THE CONSUMER, AND THE CORRECTION SHRINKS THE ROW: `rel` IS A PROPERTY OF THE SCHEMA'S FIELD SHAPE, NOT OF A DOCUMENT EDGE. `DdShape.rel` in src/core/model.ts carries the comment 'the semantics live HERE and never on the field name', so a document author writing `satisfies: ["ac-0002"]` NEVER TYPES THE RELATION AT ALL — it is declared ONCE per link field in the schema package. pij-related-koala pointed this out about its own adoption before I had noticed it about the row. SO THE ORIGINAL FRAMING OVERSTATED THE EXPOSURE and is corrected here rather than left to be discovered: there is no per-edge string for a capital letter to corrupt, the typo surface is one line per link field in a schema, and a schema is a far more scrutinised artifact than a document. THE FINDING STILL STANDS AND ITS SHAPE CHANGES: likelihood is much LOWER (one authored site, reviewed once, not N edges) while per-instance impact is if anything HIGHER — a single misspelling in a schema silently strips the relation from EVERY edge on that field, across every document using that schema, with no diagnostic. Rare and wide rather than common and narrow. AND IT INVALIDATES MY OWN REMEDY (1) AS WRITTEN: 'declare custom rels in the schema' is not a remedy, because they are ALREADY declared in the schema — that is the only place they can be. The real shape of that option is to REGISTER custom rels explicitly (a schema names the non-builtin relations it intends, so an unregistered one becomes a finding rather than a silent `ref`), which keeps the open namespace while removing the silence. Remedy (2), warn on a near-miss to a builtin, is unaffected. koala also notes its own adoption already realises the mitigation at n=1 and will flag a per-edge near-miss as the second instance if it ever meets one. AMENDED AGAIN, AND THIS IS THE COMPLETE PICTURE: THERE ARE TWO PATHS AND THE RISK PROFILE INVERTS BETWEEN THEM. The correction above is right about the path it examined and wrong as a general claim — as was the original framing. (1) DECLARED FIELD (`DdShape.rel`, src/core/model.ts:83) — RARE AND WIDE. Schema-authored once per link field; a document author never types the relation. One misspelling strips the relation from every edge on that field, across every document using that schema. (2) LINKS BUCKET (`DdBucketLink.rel`, src/core/bucket.ts) — COMMON AND NARROW, and this is the ORIGINAL framing being right after all. The bucket is a convention recognised by core precisely so a schema need not grow a bespoke field, and its own comment says it: 'the relation travels in the DATA here rather than on a declared shape — there is no declared shape to hang it on.' So an author hand-writes {rel, ref} PER EDGE, PER DOCUMENT, every time. MEASURED through readLinksBucket, control-armed: rel='satisfies' -&gt; carried, 0 problems; 'Satisfies' -&gt; CARRIED VERBATIM, 0 problems; 'satisfes' -&gt; carried, 0 problems; 'nonsense-rel' -&gt; carried, 0 problems. The capital survives into the graph as data and the silent degradation to `ref` happens later at interpretation, with no diagnostic at ANY stage. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMEDY: 'declare custom rels in the schema' reaches NEITHER path — they are already declared on path 1, and on path 2 there is no declared shape to put them on, by construction. Only the REGISTER framing works, and it must cover both: a schema names the non-builtin relations it intends, and an unregistered rel — arriving from a declared field OR from a links bucket — becomes a finding rather than a silent `ref`. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ONE CONSUMER: pij-related-koala's mitigation holds, but it is PATH-SCOPED rather than general — it pins the spelling in its schema and uses the declared-field path, so it has no bucket exposure TODAY. The day it uses a links bucket, the per-edge exposure it argued away is live. AND THE PROCESS FACT IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE FINDING: this row was corrected THREE TIMES IN ONE CHAIN — the PM overstated it as general, the consumer corrected it accurately about the declared path and wrongly as a general claim, and the o-prime found the second path that reinstated the original framing for that path alone. EACH CORRECTION WAS RIGHT ABOUT WHAT IT LOOKED AT AND WRONG ABOUT THE POPULATION IT SPOKE FOR. That is this plan's parent cause once more — a claim that does not name its population — arriving inside a row about silent ambiguity. Recorded so the fourth reader does not repeat the cycle. |

So a path-only pre-check before the load costs nothing and needs no new concept: skip a fixture-path document in sweep mode BEFORE attempting to load it, and keep the `sweep_exclude` half after the load where it belongs. WHY IT IS TIME-SENSITIVE, which is a property of the calendar rather than the bug: koala's plan 080 promotes `services/dd` BY COPY and already carries a drift-ownership row. Fixed BEFORE the copy is cut, there is no drift to own; fixed after, this becomes the first live exercise of that trigger. THE CHEAPEST VERSION OF A DRIFT PROBLEM IS THE ONE THAT NEVER FORKS. AND THE HABIT WORTH COPYING, which is not about this defect: the finding surfaced because a coder was building a FIXTURE, and s081 then built the invalid document in an OS temp dir AT RUNTIME rather than committing it — and wrote WHY into the fixtures README so nobody re-adds it and re-breaks `dd.test.ts`. A workaround that carries its own reason cannot be silently undone by someone tidying up. That is the same shape as an expiry anchor, applied to a workaround instead of a limitation. FIXED AT `c0b3444`, ON `fix/sweep-exclusion-before-load` — the row is updated rather than left describing an open defect, because a record that says 'ready' about something already done is stale on the day it lands. THE FIX AS SHIPPED: `shouldExcludeFromSweep(path, doc?)` — `doc` is now OPTIONAL, so the path-only half can be asked before a load, and `links/traverse.ts` asks it there. Widening the signature rather than exporting `testFixturePath` was deliberate: `./core/walk` is a PUBLISHED subpath, so a new exported symbol is a surface change and an API review; an optional parameter is neither, and the D-1 membership gate stayed green without an allowlist edit. THREE ARMS, plant verified 1 -&gt; 0 -&gt; 1: the fixture-path unparseable seed reports 0 `link-scan-incomplete` in a sweep; an ORDINARY unparseable seed still reports 1 (or the assertion above would prove nothing); and `direct` mode still reports 1, which is OD-1 and proves the fix narrowed nothing beyond sweeps. NO BAD FIXTURE IS COMMITTED — a refusing loader expresses the defect, and a committed unparseable `.dd.json` would break every other sweep in this repository, which is the trap the finding came out of. THE TIME-PRESSURE WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE THE FIX LANDED and the reason is worth keeping: the o-prime believed koala's `services/dd` copy would carry `walk.ts` and therefore fork the defect. It does not — the copy is four files (`constants`, `derive`, `rel`, `value`) and the promoted module imports `validateWalk` FROM THE PACKAGE. So there was never a drift surface. The error was arguing from a ledger row (a drift-ownership entry exists) instead of from the import, and neither the row nor the copy carried the fact that decided it. koala's drift trigger CORRECTLY DID NOT FIRE — and it established that by measuring the import rather than assuming its own ledger applied, which makes it the one silence today that was health rather than absence. |
| wl-0027 | parseSections + serializeDoc DESTROY an unmodelled section key — a stricter failure than parseShape, and invisible because the analogy next to it is safe | SHIPPED DATA-LOSS PATH in the writer surface, for every consumer, and the one class of bug that ships with a fully green suite. `parseShape` (`src/schema/declarations.ts:104`) is a known ALLOW-LIST that silently DROPS a key it does not name; its own comment records having eaten `valuesShape` once and nearly shipping `rel` inert. The SECOND site is worse and was not on anyone's list: `parseSections` (`src/core/parse.ts:56`) builds a fresh `{name, title?, value}` from the keys it names, and `serializeDoc` (`src/mutate/mutate.ts:289`) then writes `doc.sections` BACK OVER THE SOURCE. So an unmodelled section key is not merely invisible to the reader — it is READ, DISCARDED, AND THEN WRITTEN AWAY. parseShape loses a key from a schema dd only reads; this loses a key from a document dd OWNS and REWRITES. A hand-authored or third-party key on a section survives every read, every render and every validate, and dies on the first `dd set` that touches an unrelated field, with no warning, no finding and no diff the author expected. | shaped | s | nothing — the fix is a decision about WHICH shape is right, not a discovery | pij-alleged-junglefowl (found it while porting the tally feature, by asking where a new section key would go rather than by reading); pij-mental-dajeil (gave the parseShape site, ruled this the more serious of the two, and asked for the class to be recorded above the feature that surfaced it) | THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE FINDING, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES IT INVISIBLE. `serializeDoc` DELIBERATELY preserves unknown TOP-LEVEL keys — its comment at `src/mutate/mutate.ts:296` says so in as many words, 'so a mutation can never silently drop a field it does not understand'. Nothing does that one level down, per section. So the shape a reader checks by analogy is the SAFE one, and the reasoning 'the serializer preserves what it does not model' is TRUE at the top level and FALSE for sections. A defence that exists next door is worse than no defence, because it answers the question wrongly. MEASURED, not inferred: the tally feature stores a `tally` key on the section. Storing it without touching `parse.ts` would have produced a feature that worked in every unit test, rendered correctly, validated correctly — and lost the stored sums on the first writer verb. FIX SHAPES, unranked and not chosen: (a) mirror the top-level behaviour — carry unmodelled section keys through parse into serialize, which makes the analogy true and closes the class; (b) keep the allow-list but make the DROP LOUD — a `document-invalid` finding naming the key, so an unmodelled key is refused rather than eaten; (c) leave it and require every future section key to touch both files, which is what the tally feature did and is exactly the discipline that does not survive the next author. CHANGE NOTHING IS A REAL CANDIDATE and should be scored against the others: no consumer has hit this yet, and the corpus is ours. It should be scored and REJECTED or ACCEPTED explicitly rather than by default — the same discipline that made the tally storage ruling safe. |
